clue.text: Adam's in Cromer reviving a fellow belligerent

indicators.note: reviving something brings it back in a new form, so the letters are remade into another order

parts.note: the name taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored
taken as written; it joins the letters to be rearranged
a seaside town in Norfolk, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone called Adam recovers in the Norfolk seaside town of Cromer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a joining word placing Adam in Cromer, but its two letters belong to the fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade in arms is a soldier fighting on the same side, a fellow combatant in a war.

clue.text: Watchful one helping to hold up objectionable part

indicators.note: in a down answer, what holds something up sits beneath it, so the helper goes below
only a part of the word is wanted, here its opening pair of letters

parts.note: the first two letters of the word
a servant is someone who helps or serves

explanation.surface: An alert assistant props up the offensive bit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, alert and attentive, which is what watchful describes.

clue.text: Incite French writer quiet' ly to go

indicators.note: the letter for soft playing is told to leave, so it is removed

parts.note: Marcel Proust, French novelist
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone urges a French author to slip away quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy prints 'quiet' ly' for quietly. P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone up into action, close to incite.

clue.text: Turned red on liner deck

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it
turned round, the colour word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards
SS, steamship, the prefix on an ocean liner's name

explanation.surface: Something went red on the deck of an ocean liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' wants to be a ship's deck after 'liner'; it is the verb, to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or array, as in deck the halls, and to dress a window or a ship is the same.

clue.text: Animal with tailless body suffers contortion of the belly

indicators.note: without its tail, the word loses its last letter
contorted things are twisted out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter cut off

explanation.surface: A creature with a shortened body is suffering a twisted stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy reads 'surfers', a misread of suffers. 'Animal' looks like the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal is the adjective for the abdomen, the belly, so it means relating to the belly.

clue.text: Girl doctor supported by militants

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is supported rests on top, so the militants come underneath

parts.note: MO, medical officer, an army doctor
the IRA, Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A woman doctor has the backing of armed militants.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a female first name, and crosswords use girl to clue any woman's name.

clue.text: Twister'

parts.note: surface reading: a tornado, or a cheat who twists the truth
setter's reading: a performer who twists their own body into knots

explanation.walkthrough: One word, read literally: someone who twists. The stray quote mark is an artefact of the copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A contortionist is an acrobat who bends and twists the body into extreme positions, a literal twister.

clue.text: Pop territory?

parts.note: surface reading: the domain of pop music, the charts
setter's reading: pop as dad, so the land belonging to one's father

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' wants to be music; it is the informal word for father, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The fatherland is one's native country, the land of one's fathers, especially Germany in older usage.

clue.text: Unknown scientist gets ancient city absorbed in Old English …

indicators.note: what is absorbed in something ends up inside it, so the first pieces go within the last

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for Old English
BSc, a Bachelor of Science degree, stands for a science graduate
Ur, the Sumerian city in Mesopotamia, is crosswords' favourite ancient city

explanation.surface: A nameless scientist finds an ancient city has been swallowed up by Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy reads 'an fient city', a misread of ancient city. A science graduate and the city sit together inside the Old English abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means little known or not famous, as in an obscure poet, matching unknown.

clue.text: … a language Diana finds sort of dishy to use outside

indicators.note: the rearranged word is placed on the outside, wrapping around the name
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged into a different form

parts.note: the word taken as written, then rearranged
Di is the usual short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: Diana discovers a language that is somehow attractive, and decides to speak it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie it to the clue before, but it stands alone. 'Dishy' is British slang for good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is a Germanic language written in Hebrew script, spoken by Ashkenazi Jews.

clue.text: House supporter — risky to be otherwise!

indicators.note: to be otherwise is to take a different form, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Backing a particular house is a risky choice unless things change.
explanation.walkthrough: House means a royal dynasty here, the House of York of the Wars of the Roses, not a building or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkist backed the House of York against Lancaster in the fifteenth-century Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Thanks to rubbish game …

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone says thanks for a terrible game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a card game played with a special pack, best known now for fortune-telling but long played as a game.

clue.text: … some crumpled in flash display on the rugger field

definitions.note: names where the player is found, not the player

indicators.note: the short run of letters sits inside the rearranged word
a display puts things on show in a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: the word taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: only some of the following word is wanted, its opening run of letters

parts.note: the opening four letters of the word

explanation.surface: Some crumpled item shows up in a flashy show at a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join it to the clue before, but it stands alone. Rugger is British slang for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum-half is the rugby player who feeds the ball into the scrum, a position found on every rugby pitch.

clue.text: Quantities "are badly needed for writing

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Large quantities are urgently required for someone's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reams are large amounts, from the ream as a measure of paper, as in reams of notes.

clue.text: Reads up to disperse

parts.note: the three words taken as written, then scattered

explanation.surface: Someone studies a subject until they are ready to scatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disperse' does double duty: it defines the answer and tells you to scatter the letters of 'Reads up to' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out is to scatter or extend over a wider area, which is what disperse means.

clue.text: Ligament broken — new starter enters the line-up

indicators.note: what enters goes inside, so the single letter is placed within the rearranged word
a broken thing is in pieces, and these letters are put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sports injury report: a torn ligament means a new player comes into the team.
explanation.definitionFit: An alignment is an arrangement in a line, and also a grouping of allies, as a line-up is.

clue.text: Dry wine for ventilation?

definitions.note: a punning reading of the answer, a port for air, not a dictionary sense

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A dry wine is recommended for freshening the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: split in two, the answer reads as an opening, a port, for air; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the answer is an air port, an opening that lets air through, which is what ventilation needs.

clue.text: A step forward in one's education — an alarm clock?

definitions.text: A step forward in one's education
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a revelation that teaches something new
second meaning, playful: something that literally gets the sleeper's lids up

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a joke on the literal sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation; taken literally it is anything that makes you open your eyes, like an alarm.

clue.text: Explain or bury prettier half

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: half of a word means taking only its front portion, the first four of its eight letters

parts.note: the first half of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A choice: explain things, or bury the better-looking half of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to make the meaning of something clear, to explain or translate it.

clue.text: Vassal in Belgium

definitions.note: a place found there, not a word meaning 'in Belgium'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Liège, a city in eastern Belgium

explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a liege is more often the lord, but it also named the subject bound to him; the second half points to the Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Liege, as a noun, can mean a feudal subject bound to serve a superior, which is what a vassal is.

clue.text: Fairly near — on raft, perhaps

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
this is a reverse clue: 'off' is a common rearrangement signal, and 'perhaps' asks for that signal itself to be written in

explanation.surface: Someone drifting on a raft is reckoned to be fairly close to land.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a cryptic instruction: its first two words, with the third as the signal to rearrange, give back 'on raft'. 'Perhaps' marks that the clue works backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not far off is close by, at no great distance, which is what fairly near means.

clue.text: Reset in concise terms

indicators.note: the word is set again in other terms, a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written; its own sense, set again, also hints at rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to rewrite something more briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reset' is both the letters to move and a hint to move them; 'in concise terms' reads as one phrase, but only 'concise' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and to the point, using few words, which is what concise means.

clue.text: From Rome — a portmanteau in Somerset

definitions.note: names the place where the town is, not a synonym

indicators.note: a portmanteau word blends two words, so their shared middle letters appear only once

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it shares its first three letters with the end of the word before

explanation.surface: Something from Rome, a large travelling bag, turns up in the English county of Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: A portmanteau is also an old-fashioned suitcase, which the surface uses. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Frome is a market town in the English county of Somerset, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Little rogue elephant starts drive

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous creature, a little rogue

indicators.note: the starts of a word are its opening letters, here the first two

parts.note: the first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A small rogue elephant begins to move off.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward, as in impelled to act.

clue.text: Casting obtained from casting others

indicators.note: what is obtained from words is taken out of them, a run of letters within

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A cast is made from the castings of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' first looks like choosing actors; it is a piece of cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of metal cast in a mould, so it is a casting.

clue.text: Versatile actor takes us back in medieval garment

indicators.note: taken back, the short word runs from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards

indicators.note: something versatile takes many forms, so the letters can be shaped into a new one

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An all-round actor brings us back to the past in a medieval costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Versatile actor' reads as a performer; 'versatile' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcoat was a loose tunic worn over armour by medieval knights, often bearing their arms.

clue.text: Inquiry or note by un known writer

definitions.note: an organon is a tool of inquiry rather than an inquiry itself

parts.note: taken as written
G is one of the musical notes A to G
anon, short for anonymous, signs a piece by an unidentified author

explanation.surface: Someone queries a note left by an anonymous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy splits unknown into 'un known'. Organon was Aristotle's name for logic as the instrument of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: An organon is a system of principles used for philosophical or scientific investigation, an instrument of inquiry.

clue.text: Musical team opposing the East is conservative

parts.note: west is the compass point facing east
a side is a sports team
the contraction of is, as in it's
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A music group that stands against the East turns out to be politically conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical team' reads as a band; 'Musical' alone is the definition. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: West Side Story is the 1957 Bernstein and Sondheim stage musical, a New York retelling of Romeo and Juliet.
